Governmental funds are reported by function. Enterprise funds (water, sewer, electric, liquor stores and others) count their operating revenue and expenses with depreciation left out and capital outlay counted when paid, plus debt payments.
Borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
General government, housing and redevelopment, economic development and conservation of natural resources count as overhead.
Debt is bonds, other long-term debt and short-term debt outstanding at year end, as reported.
Political money is not scored: Minnesota county candidates file campaign finance reports with their county auditor, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Lake County Sheriff's Office spent $2500 on its unmanned aerial vehicle program in 2023 and flew a drone three times without a warrant that year.

Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Lake County.
Minnesota townships (towns) govern the areas outside cities, mostly maintaining township roads; many contract with a city or fire district for fire protection.

Governmental funds are reported by function. Enterprise funds (water, sewer, electric, liquor stores and others) count their operating revenue and expenses with depreciation left out and capital outlay counted when paid, plus debt payments.
Borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
General government, housing and redevelopment, economic development and conservation of natural resources count as overhead.
Debt is bonds, other long-term debt and short-term debt outstanding at year end, as reported.
Political money is not scored: Minnesota local candidates file campaign finance reports with their city or township clerk, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
Cameras: no license-plate cameras are mapped inside Silver Creek Township's borders in OpenStreetMap as of 2026-10-18.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Minnesota yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
